Bastien Sauty is a researcher in Mechanical Engineering and Biomechanics, specializing in the mechanical modeling of complex materials undergoing large deformations. His research focuses on developing computational tools to analyze the biomechanical response of living tissues.

---

He earned his *Ph.D. in Mechanical Engineering* in 2026 through a joint doctoral program between *École des Mines de Saint-Étienne* and *Università degli Studi di Roma -- Tor Vergata*. His doctoral research investigated the multiscale modeling of arterial tissue, specifically analyzing microstructural heterogeneity, local strain and stress distributions, and the impact of cellular contraction on global tissue behavior.

Prior to his doctorate, he studied Mechanical Engineering at École Normale Supérieure Paris-Saclay and earned an M.Sc. in Biomechanics from Arts et Métiers Institute of Technology (ENSAM). His foundational research explores multiphysics and multiscale interactions, with a focus on cellular contraction, osmotic swelling, and collagen uncrimping.

---

In September 2026, Bastien joined the Laboratoire de Mécanique des Solides (LMS) at École Polytechnique. His current research focuses on the poroelastic modeling of the cornea to study how microstructure influences osmotic diffusion and mechanical response, ultimately aiming to improve corneal mechanics modeling and refine surgical planning for refractive procedures.
